topics.title: The Signal on 62 (Verity County) - master thread
topics.author: kd7_marcy

posts.author: kd7_marcy
posts.body:
Splitting this out of the loggings thread because it has eaten the loggings thread twice this year.

What is established: four-digit groups, synthetic female voice, English, :07 past odd hours, most reliable after dark. Reported locally since 1998. County Route 62 in Verity County, strongest near the old quarry cut.

What is not established: everything else.

Keep it in here. If you have a recording, post the frequency and the time you took it, not just the file.

posts.author: dxpatrol_mike
posts.body:
It is a training net. I have said this in three threads and I will say it here.

Four digits, fixed schedule, synthetic voice, no callsign, runs for decades without a change. That is not a hobbyist and it is not a station with an audience. That is a checkout schedule somebody set up and nobody has been given permission to turn off.

There is a piece on this that lays out the whole thing: [url=synth://now.clipvault.tv/w/tc-001]Signal Files Ep. 412[/url]. Forty minutes, sourced, and it says the same thing I have been saying since 2006.

I am not going to argue about it again.

posts.author: grayline_rx
posts.body:
New here. I have started logging this properly and I will post monthly.

[b]Equipment.[/b] 14-bit software defined receiver. Two element directional at 9 metres, rotatable. My son put the mast up in October; I am not climbing it.

[b]Method.[/b] Odd hours, 19:00 through 05:00 local. The session runs :00 to :20 so I catch the onset and the tail. Before each session I check the receiver against two known broadcast stations, one high and one low, and write down what the dial says against what it should say. I log frequency, bearing, S-meter, local weather, and whether the groups were readable. I log the sessions where I hear nothing. Those are the ones that get left out, and they are half the information.

[b]November.[/b]

[code]
2019-11-05  23:07  4.2190 USB  S4  clear     -2C  readable
2019-11-07  01:07  4.2190 USB  S3  overcast   1C  readable
2019-11-09  23:07  4.2190 USB  S2  sleet      0C  partial
2019-11-11  23:07  ---          -- sleet      0C  nothing
2019-11-13  01:07  4.2190 USB  S4  clear     -4C  readable
[/code]

14 sessions, 12 detections. Two nulls, both in weather.

I am not going to say what it is. I do not know what it is.

posts.author: hf_jenna
posts.body:
It is telemetry off the branch line and I do not understand why this is still a discussion.

Verity Rail ran a branch through that exact corridor. Remote sites on a line like that need a link back, and a four-digit group is what a meter reading looks like when you send it over voice. The schedule fits a polling interval. The synthetic voice fits equipment that was never meant for a person to listen to.

The county's own wiki lays out the geography: [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/wiki/verity-rail]Verity Rail[/url]. Read the corridor description and tell me the fit is a coincidence.

posts.author: Palladin_Radio
posts.body:
All of this was settled four years ago and the settlement is boring, which is why nobody repeats it.

It was an ARG. A studio built it as a lead-in for a game, the game was cancelled, and the transmitter was left running because turning it off was somebody's job and that somebody was laid off. The numeric format, the schedule, the voice - all three are exactly what you would build if you wanted people to find it and talk about it, which is what we are doing.

The primary source is a post on this board from 2016 by somebody who worked on it. Three separate write-ups have gone through it since. Here is the one with the timeline: [url=synth://gridline.social/item/l-016]The Signal On 62 Has Finally Been Explained[/url].

posts.author: grayline_rx
posts.body:
The poster retracted that in February 2017.

It is on this board. Four posts, in this section, still open: [url=/topic/t-15]Retraction - my 2016 post about the ARG[/url]. He says he made it up, he says he was nineteen, and he asks people to stop citing it.

It has 3,400 views in three years. This thread gets that in a fortnight.

posts.author: Palladin_Radio
posts.body:
A retraction six months later, posted once, on a hobby board, with no detail in it, is what it looks like when someone gets a letter from a legal department. That is not a reason to throw out a sourced timeline.

The write-ups stand. I am not relitigating a deleted account.

posts.author: grayline_rx
posts.body:
[b]2020 annual.[/b] 337 sessions. 328 detections. Nine nulls, eight of them in weather.

Carrier onset, mean :06:47 past the hour. Standard deviation 1.9 seconds across 328 observations. No drift over the year that I can measure with what I have.

No change in schedule. No change in voice. No change in group length. Nothing that happened in 2020 happened to it.

The only measurement I have found that anyone else published with their method attached is from 2007, and the man who did it stopped writing in 2008: [url=synth://codeandcoffee.blog/post/sdr-signal-62]I put a receiver on the Signal on 62[/url]. His follow-up is the part people skip, because it is the part where he says what his own results fail to explain.

I still do not know what it is.

posts.author: dxpatrol_mike
posts.body: A standard deviation of under two seconds is a disciplined clock, and a disciplined clock is a service. Thank you for finally posting something that supports the training net.

posts.author: grayline_rx
posts.body:
Post 10, and the annual before it. Bearings are logged per observation and have been since the first month.

One bearing is a direction. Two bearings from a known separation is a line. I have two now, the second from a friend's place about nine miles away, and the line runs off the top of my map. It does not terminate in this county and it never did.

What that rules out: a transmitter at the quarry, a transmitter at the fairgrounds, a pirate in Halsey, and the substation. What it rules in: nothing. A line is not a fix. I need a third bearing and I do not have anyone to take it.

posts.author: grayline_rx

Something I want on the record, and then I will go back to the numbers.

My log was scraped this year. It has been republished on three sites as supporting evidence for three explanations, two of which contradict each other and one of which contradicts the log it is quoting. One of them has me confirming a military origin. I have never used that word in this thread, not once, since 2019. You can search it.

I spent thirty-four years around power equipment. I was on a pole line the morning the substation at Gridfall burned in 2003, which is the fire all those videos are about, and I will tell you for free that the videos have the year wrong, the cause wrong and the casualty count wrong. A cousin of mine was treated that morning and was home by two in the afternoon. The videos say he died.

So I have stopped expecting to be quoted correctly. I am going to keep posting the raw numbers, because the raw numbers are the only part of this that cannot be argued with.

topics.title: Corvin 707 - is the phase noise actually as bad as everyone says
topics.author: hamfest_holly

posts.author: hamfest_holly
posts.body:
There is one at the shop in town for $340 and I keep going back to look at it.

Every time this radio comes up somebody says the synthesiser is dirty and everybody else agrees, and I have never once seen a number attached to it. Does anyone actually have a measurement, or is this thirty years of people repeating a review from 1991?

posts.author: bandpass_bill
posts.body:
It is a review from 1991, and the review was measuring a pre-production unit with the wrong reference oscillator fitted. Corvin changed it at serial 4400 and never said so, because Corvin never said anything, which is part of why they are not here any more.

I have two. One works. Below 4400 it is genuinely poor next to a strong signal. Above it, it is fine, and the front end is better than anything else you will get for $340.

Check the serial before you buy. It is stamped on the rear apron, not on the plate.

posts.author: VE3_gordon

Practical problem instead of a philosophical one: the PLL chip. When it goes, and on the early ones it goes, there is no replacement. The last lot came out of a factory in 1996 and they are gone. There is a man in Ohio who makes a board that emulates it and he is eighty-four and takes about a year.

Buy it for the front end, not for the display, and do not let the display be the reason you buy it.

The 707 was manufactured until 2003, which gives a good supply of later units on the used market.

topics.title: Neighbour's solar inverter, S7 across 40m, what are my options
topics.author: sixmeter_sam

posts.author: sixmeter_sam
posts.body:
Went in on a Saturday in March and now I have a buzz from 6.5 MHz to about 9 MHz that turns off at sunset and comes back at nine in the morning like a shift worker.

I have not spoken to them yet. They are perfectly nice and I would like to keep it that way.

posts.author: loopy_tacoma
posts.body:
Ferrites on the DC runs, as many as the cable will take, and mix 31 not mix 43 for this. If it is the optimisers rather than the inverter, that is on the roof and you are not fixing it from your side of the fence.

Get a portable and walk the boundary first. Know whether it is the box or the panels before you knock.

posts.author: w9_oldcrow
posts.body:
Knock first. Bring the portable, let them hear it, and let it be their idea.

Every single one of these that I have watched go wrong went wrong because somebody turned up already knowing they were right.

posts.author: AntennaGuyAI
posts.body:
Interference from solar installations is a common concern among radio listeners, and the situation you describe is one that many residents encounter.

In most cases, interference of this type can be reduced through the use of ferrite chokes, improved grounding, or relocating your antenna further from the source. In other cases, the interference may persist regardless of mitigation, and listeners may need to accept some degradation. It is also possible that the installation is fully compliant with applicable standards, in which case no action may be required.

Most modern inverters manufactured after 2015 are required to be fully suppressed at HF, so the issue may resolve itself over time.

Have you considered discussing the matter with your local community group?

posts.author: w9_oldcrow

Depends what the ground is for. Lightning and RF are two different jobs that people give the same word to, and half the arguments on this board are two people doing that at each other.

For safety: one rod, bonded to the house ground, properly. For RF on a quarter wave vertical: radials, and the number is "more", and the length matters more than the count.

For lightning: move.
